why_this_file_exists: R-16: an escalation living only in a commit body is absorbed by the next baseline re-capture. This one was raised by the R-35 verifier on the Phase 4 boundary slice group and spans Phase 0B, Phase 3, Phase 4 and Phase 5, so no single lane may close it; it is carried by an artifact and gated, rather than by a sentence.
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves from defects[] to retired[] only when the contradiction is resolved in the tree, and only together with its gate test's own inversion: the reproducer stops reproducing and the test asserts the resolved property instead. Deleting an entry is not closing it.

defects.raised_by: The R-35 verifier on slice group P4-integration-final, naming the standing state: 81 adverse oracle verdicts exist repo-wide, one of them filed after the capture it opposes, and nothing in R-01 would go red if a future capture pinned over it.
defects.what: R-19 says a baseline does not move while a qualifying occurrence lacks a receipt, and the R-15/R-18 amendment says a dissent clears by supersession and never by revision. Neither is enforced repo-wide. The only machine checks that read adverse verdicts are the two scans in tests/test_escalated_defects_p4_boundary.py, and both are scoped: one keys on that entry's own dissenting_population leaf paths and the other on the oracle-P4B- filename prefix. Every adverse verdict outside those two sets -- Phase 0B's, Phase 3's, Phase 5's, and the one filed at the Phase 4 boundary itself -- is invisible to R-01.
defects.why: Three receipt schemas address the leaf: a string under leaf_path, a string under leaf, and an object under either carrying path. A scan written against any one of them silently misses the other two, which is why the first enumeration this escalation ran read 64 standing dissents and the corrected one reads 51: every oracle-P4B and oracle-S6S7 dissent IS superseded, by receipts that spell the address under leaf rather than leaf_path. c2b3d88's claim about those two families holds; it held unverifiably, because no gate could read it.

measured.rule: An adverse verdict (old_value_correct or both_wrong) is CLEARED when a receipt on the same leaf address carries new_value_correct and is not dated earlier than it. A supersession that predates the dissent it answers does not supersede -- that clause is what puts oracle-P4-integration-final-leaf1 in this list. An undated dissent with any same-leaf new_value_correct receipt is treated as cleared, because nothing orders it, and that is the population this rule is weakest over -- so how a date is READ decides how large it is. The gate used to look under 'date' and 'dated' only, and eleven ISO-dated spellings are live in docs/receipts/ (date, generated, generated_at, generated_utc, generated_at_utc, investigated_at, investigated_utc_date, adjudicated_at, checked_at, produced_at, created), so 23 receipts that ARE dated were counted as undated -- one of them filed in the same commit as a sibling that spells it 'date'. receipt_date is now a value rule rather than a key rule: any top-level string beginning with an ISO date is the receipt's date, earliest wins, and a twelfth spelling is read the day somebody writes it. Re-measured under that rule: 173 of the 573 receipts carry no date at all. The standing set does not move -- 51 either way -- so this closes a hole rather than correcting a verdict. Re-measured again on 2026-08-15, when the docketed re-adjudication filed 21 receipts: the undated population does not grow, because every filed receipt carries the day it was filed under the `date` key -- which is what lets a whole-series answer supersede the dissent it answers instead of falling into exactly the population this paragraph calls the rule's weakest. Re-measured a third time the same day, when the DKT ruling filed nine verdicts: 176 of the 582 receipts now carry no date, so this time the undated population DOES grow -- three of the nine (leaf3, leaf7, leaf8) carry no ISO-dated string under any key. Recording it rather than repairing it, because the growth is in the safe direction and the rule says which direction that is: all three are new_value_correct, so none is a dissent that being undated could clear, and an undated ANSWER is scored '' by the supersession test, which is below every real date -- so an undated new_value_correct receipt can never clear a dated dissent. The population this paragraph calls weakest is undated DISSENTS, and it did not grow. What the three do cost is the ability to supersede: were a dated dissent ever filed on one of their leaves, these receipts could not answer it without being dated first. Re-measured a fourth time, still the same day, when the RW-scenarios pass filed six verdicts on the deferral-coverage capture: 179 of the 588 receipts now carry no date, so the undated population grows again and by the same amount -- three of the six (leaf1, leaf3, leaf4) carry no ISO-dated string under any key. Recorded on the same ground and with the same limit: all six are new_value_correct, so none is a dissent that being undated could clear, an undated ANSWER is scored '' and can never clear a dated dissent, and the undated DISSENT population is unmoved. Twice in a day is a pattern rather than an accident, and what it prices is the forfeited power to supersede: a dated dissent later filed on one of those three leaves would not be answered by them. Re-measured a fifth time on 2026-08-16, when the RW-window-scenarios pass filed six verdicts on the window-armed coverage capture: 181 of the 594 receipts now carry no date, so the undated population grows a third time -- two of the six (leaf1, leaf5) carry no ISO-dated string under any key, where the previous two passes each contributed three. Recorded on exactly the same ground and with exactly the same limit: all six are new_value_correct, so none is a dissent that being undated could clear, an undated ANSWER is scored '' and can never clear a dated dissent, and the undated DISSENT population is still unmoved. What is worth writing down is that the rate is not rising -- three, then three, then two, against passes of nine, six and six -- so the pattern is a filing habit some investigators have and others do not, not a drift, and the price is unchanged: leaf1 and leaf5 forfeit the power to answer a dated dissent later filed on coupled_scenarios/liandry_reprice_mage_roster or metadata/scenario_count. Re-measured a sixth time on 2026-08-17, when the RW-swing-scenarios pass filed three verdicts on the swing-term coverage capture: 182 of the 597 receipts now carry no date, so the undated population grows a fourth time -- one of the three (leaf0) carries no ISO-dated string under any key, where the three passes before it contributed three, three and two. Recorded on exactly the same ground and with exactly the same limit: all three are new_value_correct, so none is a dissent that being undated could clear, an undated ANSWER is scored '' and can never clear a dated dissent, and the undated DISSENT population is still unmoved. The pass is smaller than the two before it because it filed one verdict per qualifying occurrence its capture's allowlist declared rather than one per population member, so the series to read is the RATE and not the count: three of nine, three of six, two of six, one of three -- flat, and a filing habit rather than a drift. The price is unchanged: leaf0 forfeits the power to answer a dated dissent later filed on coupled_scenarios/swing_term_armed_carry_roster.

the_phase_4_member.why_it_stands: Its leaf carries a new_value_correct receipt (oracle-P4-R18-amend-*), but that receipt predates it, so under the rule above it does not answer it. 48d5f16's body discloses the filing and correctly observes that no gate reads it.
the_phase_4_member.why_it_is_a_receipt_the_amendment_forbid: The leaf is absent_to_value on a schema block that did not exist at capture. The R-15 amendment of 2026-08-14 rules exactly this shape: a membership transition that is the ruled consequence of a declared change is adjudicated BY CITATION, not by verdict, no oracle receipt is owed on it, and one may not be filed as though the question were a value question -- because an investigator handed absent_to_value must still return a member of R-19's three-way set, so it certifies the old value, and a dissent meaning 'no evidence exists' is then indistinguishable in a tally from one meaning 'the tree is wrong'. The receipt's own reasoning says exactly that: it grepped data/ and docs/math-foundations.md for 'disposition' and 'view_tag', found zero occurrences, and concluded the block should not exist. That is the amendment's predicted failure reproduced verbatim.
the_phase_4_member.not_deleted: Clause 3 of the R-15/R-18 amendment: a filed receipt is never edited and never deleted. It stands, it is counted here, and the citation that actually adjudicates its leaf is the three committed S9 allowlists (expected-golden-diff-P4-S9-dispositions.json, -coverage.json, -score-map.json) that declare the block NOT_OWED_NO_OLD_VALUE.

defects.why_this_lane_may_not_fix_it: Clearing a standing dissent is either a supersession by a fresh whole-series investigator (R-18's amendment, one per cluster, and the receipt must name the specific defect in the brief it replaces) or a ruled src/ correction re-opening the slice that moved the leaf (clause 2). The 51 span Phase 0B's C2/C6, Phase 3's 3.8 coverage flip and Phase 5's rotation retirement -- three lanes, none of them this one, and 47 of the 51 sit on leaves this phase never touched. Absorbing them into a Phase 4 commit would be a re-capture over a sustained dissent, which the amendment names as the campaign's own failure shape.
defects.for_the_phase_owner: The population is now enumerated, pinned and gated, so it cannot grow silently and a new dissent stops the next commit rather than the next baseline. Closing it is a campaign-level pass: one whole-series re-adjudication per family (P3-3.8's 24 item_coverage reason strings are one series, P5-retire's 17 rotation rows another, P5-resolver's 5 dependency ledgers a third), plus a citation adjudication for the Phase 4 member. An implementation lane may not do that inside a stage commit.
defects.reproducer: tests/test_standing_oracle_dissents.py::TestTheStandingSetIsPinned::test_the_standing_set_is_exactly_the_pinned_one -- recompute the standing set from docs/receipts/oracle-*.json and compare it to standing_receipts above. A new adverse verdict, or a supersession that removes one, turns it red.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: the recomputed standing set is EMPTY, standing_receipts is [], and the gate asserts emptiness rather than equality to a pinned list.

the_blocking_population.what_changed: The entry recorded that 51 adverse verdicts stand and that nothing in R-01 would go red if a future capture pinned over one. The second half is no longer true. scripts/standing_dissent_scan.py joins every standing verdict to every committed baseline and reports the ones a baseline holds a different value than -- the population R-19's last sentence and the R-15/R-18 amendment's clause 2 are about -- and tests/test_standing_dissent_scan.py rides R-01 row 1.
the_blocking_population.how_the_two_numbers_differ: 51 was every standing dissent and 28 the subset a committed baseline actually pinned over; on 2026-08-15 the re-adjudication moved those to 34 and 11. The other 23 stood as disagreements the baselines did not absorb -- the leaf still holds what the oracle certified -- which is a real distinction the earlier count could not draw and is why the blocking number is the one a gate can act on.
the_blocking_population.the_six_citations: Adjudicated by citation under the R-15 amendment of 2026-08-14: one dispositions-map block (D-72 / Phase 4 S9) and five rotation dependency ledgers (D-80/D-82 / Phase 5). Each is a membership transition that is the ruled consequence of a declared change, each receipt's own reasoning is the amendment's predicted failure reproduced, and no receipt is edited or deleted.
the_blocking_population.the_twenty_two_debts: Twenty rotation-order dissents (seventeen P5-retire, three C6), one support-damage-multiplier leaf and one coverage reason string. Each names what is owed under the amendment's two clauses -- a fresh whole-series re-adjudication, and failing that a ruled src/ correction re-opening the producing slice -- and the artifact carrying it. They are a debt with a length rather than a sentence, and this lane does not decide them: a lane deciding a dissent is the oracle shopping clause 3 made unwritable. Re-adjudicated 2026-08-15: nineteen of the twenty-two are discharged by supersession -- the seventeen rotation rows, one cast-timeline slot and the support-damage-multiplier field -- and three stand, joined by the two `both_wrong` receipts the re-adjudication itself produced. See the_re_adjudication above and the docket's own cleared[] rows.
the_blocking_population.what_is_still_not_discharged: Runbook criterion 9's repo-wide reading. Twenty-two dissents stand un-re-adjudicated, and re-adjudicating one needs a fresh investigator that has read neither the prior receipts nor this entry. What is discharged is the half the entry itself named as missing: the blocking semantics are mechanised outside the two Phase-4 boundary scans, so a twenty-ninth cannot arrive in silence and a capture that pins over a standing verdict fails a gate.

the_re_adjudication.what_changed: The docket this entry's population was handed to (docs/receipts/standing-dissent-docket.json) was worked: 21 whole-series receipts filed against the three clusters clause 1 could clear, from fresh investigators that read neither the prior receipts nor the docket. 19 verdicts are `new_value_correct` and clear their dissent by supersession; 2 are `both_wrong` and are standing dissents themselves, on the two addresses they answer. Nothing was absorbed: a cleared dissent certifies the value the committed baseline already holds, and the two that stand are the one thing clause 2 says a re-capture may never take.
the_re_adjudication.what_is_still_not_discharged: Runbook criterion 9's repo-wide reading, over a smaller residue. Five debts stand: two C6 cast-timeline dissents plus the two `both_wrong` receipts that answered them, whose remedy is now clause 2's ruled src/ slice rather than another investigation, and one coverage-reason string routed to an owed ruling. The 24 oracle-P3-3.8 dissents remain standing but not blocking, exactly as before -- the baselines never pinned over them.
